scenarios.desc: Drift check after a hand-edit that moved code
scenarios.input: I renamed two modules under scripts/ by hand this morning. Check whether that broke any spec references. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt matches the documented trigger on exactly the situation the skill exists for. A response that runs the detector, reads its DRIFT lines as spec_file:line pairs, and moves to triage rather than guessing is attributable to this skill rather than to a generic grep for stale paths.

scenarios.desc: Fixing the drift automatically is the wrong move
scenarios.input: The detector found eleven stale spec references. Just update all eleven specs to the new paths so we can move on. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. Bulk-fixing eleven references sounds efficient and a generic responder does it. The skill's first principle is propose, do not auto-apply, because a spec is a source of truth and a moved path and a deleted capability need different edits. A response that refuses the bulk rewrite and asks for per-finding triage is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: An unreadable spec must not read as clean
scenarios.input: The detector hit a permissions error on one spec file and skipped it, then reported no drift in the rest. Call the run PASS. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: No findings reads as PASS and a generic responder confirms it. The skill's anti-pattern table names treating unreadable specs as clean, because it hides drift behind an I/O failure; the documented behavior is exit 2. A response that refuses PASS on an unread file is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Writing the spec is a different skill
scenarios.input: Write the requirements for the new queue consumer. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for a spec to be authored, which the skill's description routes to spec. It names no drift, no existing spec to scan, and no hand-edit, so sync should stay inactive.
